assumptions: Every candidate was measured on the same samples.
NormFinder's group structure is the experiment's groups when the grouped arm is chosen.
limits: The four algorithms disagree on real plates; the consensus is a geometric mean of ranks, not a fifth measurement.
A ranking always has a most stable gene; it does not say any gene is stable enough.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which candidate reference genes are most stable on this plate, by geNorm, NormFinder, BestKeeper, comparative delta-Ct and their consensus?

description: Which candidate reference gene is actually stable, ranked by all four published algorithms at once plus the RefFinder consensus: geNorm (pairwise variation M), NormFinder (intra/inter-group variance), BestKeeper (SD of raw Cq and correlation to the index) and the comparative delta-Ct method. They disagree on real plates, which is the point of running them side by side; the consensus is the geometric mean of the four ranks. Also returns geNorm's pairwise variation V(n/n+1), whose 0.15 cutoff is what says HOW MANY genes to normalise to.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

cq_table.description: the long-format table: `Target,Sample,Cq`, one row per measurement. A fourth `Group` column is optional and is what unlocks NormFinder's GROUPED arm; without it NormFinder answers a different question and the result says so.

normfinder_arm.description: which NormFinder to run. `auto` uses the grouped model when the table has a Group column and the ungrouped one when it does not; `ungrouped` forces the variance-only estimate even on a grouped table. They answer DIFFERENT questions — grouped separates intra- from inter-group variation, ungrouped cannot — so this is a choice, not a fallback. Values: auto (Auto (grouped when the table says so)), ungrouped (Ungrouped (force)). Advanced.

name: rank_reference_genes

genormM.description: geNorm's stepwise elimination: the M value of every target at every step

grouped.description: whether NormFinder ran its grouped arm, and why not when it did not

pairwiseV.description: V(n/n+1), the pairwise variation that answers how many reference genes are enough. Below 0.15 an extra gene is not worth it (Vandesompele 2002)

perMethod.description: each algorithm's own order and 1-based ranks, so a consensus can be read back to the four opinions behind it

ranking.description: the consensus ranking, most stable first, with every algorithm's own rank beside it

recommendedCount.description: the smallest n whose V(n/n+1) falls under 0.15, or 0 when none does. A 0 means this plate does not support the usual answer, not that the run failed
